title: WPMS/3481/2019 of NEELAM AGARWAL Vs ANIL KUMAR AGARWAL

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition No.3481 of 2019 (M/S)
Smt. Neelam Agarwal ....Petitioner
Vs.
Anil Kumar Agarwal and another ....Respondent
Advocate : Mr. Bhagwat Mehra, Advocate for the petitioner.
 Mr. Akhil Kumar Sah, Advocate for the respondents.
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
 The petitioner has filed this writ petition praying for the
following reliefs:-
"i. To issue a writ order or direction in the nature of
certiorari to call for the record and to quash the
impugned orders dated 07.09.2019 and 23.10.2019
passed by the Court of Learned Principal Judge, Family
Court, Nainital in Case No.264 of 2015 (Anil Kumar
Agarwal vs. Smt. Neelam Agarwal) (Annexure No.16
and 21 respectively to the writ petition).
ii. To issue a writ order or direction in the nature of
mandamus restraining the Court of Learned Principal
Judge, Family Court, Nainital from proceeding further in
Case No.264 of 2015 (Anil Kumar Agarwal vs. Smt.
Neelam Agarwal), till complete and actual payment of
interim maintenance to the petitioner, as ordered vide
order dated 24.07.2017.
iii. To issue any other suitable writ, order or direction
which this Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper in the
circumstances of the case.
iv. To award the cost of the writ petition in favour of
the petitioner."
2. The impugned order, which is under challenge, was rendered
by the Principal Judge, Family Court Nainital, in Case No.264 of 2015,
Anil Kumar Agarwal vs. Smt. Neelam Agarwal. By virtue of the impugned
orders, which has been put to challenge, the petitioner's husband was

2
directed to deposit the amount of Rs. 3,56,900/-. By the second order,
which has been put to challenge that is 23.10.2019, the
defendant/petitioner's application Paper No.26 (Ga), which was preferred
for the purposes of enabling, her to cross examine the witnesses and to set
aside the order dated 07.09.2019, directing to proceed ex-parte against her
has been rejected.
3. As against the aforesaid two impugned orders, when the writ
petition was preferred, there was an interim order granted by this Court on
14.11.2019, leaving it open for the petitioner herein to file an application
for withdrawal of the amount, which had already deposited by the
respondent no.1, before the court below towards the maintenance and if an
appropriate recourse has not been adopted by the petitioner to get the
money withdrawn, it is rather she who, has to be claimed it, not the Court
neither the respondent could be held responsible for her inaction.
4. Considering the aspect of directing to proceed ex-parte, there
was yet another interim order, which was rendered on 12.02.2020, granted
by this Court restraining the proceedings to proceed ex-parte as against the
petitioner.
5. Today, when the matter was taken up, the very opening
argument extended by the learned counsel for the respondent/plaintiff to
proceedings before the court below had made a statement that the amount
as directed to be deposited before the court below, he has already deposited
by way of a cheque into the accounts of the court, which is still lying there.
6. The second argument of the counsel for the respondent is that
the order dated 07.09.2019, rejecting the application for recall to set aside
the order of proceeding ex-parte that may be allowed and the order of

3
07.09.2019, may be recalled and the petitioner may be permitted to contest
the matter on merits.
7. Looking to the candid submissions which has been made by
the counsel for the respondent, this writ petition is being allowed with a
slight modification to the order dated 07.09.2020, that the closure of the
opportunity of the petitioner would stand recall and the order to proceed
ex-parte, is hereby set aside in order to enable the petitioner to participate
in the proceeding before the court below on its own merits. As far as the
controversy pertaining to the deposits made and particularly in the light of
the interim order already granted by the Coordinate Bench of this Court, it
would be open for the petitioner to withdraw the amount already deposited
and in case if there is any controversy pertaining to the insufficiency of an
amount, which has been deposited as per the perception of the petitioner,
she may raise her grievance before the court below itself.
8. Considering the fact, that the controversy is emanating from
the proceedings under Section 13 of the Hindu Marriage Act, the Principal
Judge, Family Court, Nainital, is requested to decide the proceedings of
Case No.264 of 2015 Anil Kumar Agarwal vs. Smt. Neelam Agarwal,
itself as expeditiously as possible, but not later than the period as
prescribed under Section 21 B of the Hindu Marriage Act.
9. The parties are directed to appear before the learned court
below on 22.03.2021.
10. Subject to the above observations, the writ petition stands
partially allowed.
